title: Data detectives
goal: I can find the mean, a missing value from the mean, and compare the mean with the median and mode.

learn.intro: The mean is the total divided by how many values there are. It is the level you get when the towers are made equal. Total = mean × how many. One very large or very small value can pull the mean away from a typical value.

example.problem: Five friends collect shells: Ali 8, Mei 3, Siti 12, Ben 5 and Kumar 7. Find the mean number of shells.
steps: Divide by how many values there are: 35 ÷ 5 = 7.
Check by levelling. The towers above 7 have 1 + 5 = 6 extra shells. The towers below 7 are 4 + 2 = 6 short.

howto.title: How to work with a mean
steps: Add all the values. A value of 0 still counts.
Divide the total by how many values there are.
Missing value: total = mean × how many, then take away the values you know.
Median is the middle value in order. Mode is the most common value.

try.text: The mean of 4 numbers is 12. Three of them are 9, 15 and 10. The 4th number is {b}.
try.explanation: The total of 4 numbers is 4 × 12 = 48. The 3 known numbers add to 9 + 15 + 10 = 34. The 4th number is 48 − 34 = 14.

items.text: Find the mean of each list.
Move blocks from tall towers to short towers until all towers are equal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The mean height is {b} blocks.

parts.label: b
parts.text: {b} blocks must move from the tall towers to the short towers.

items.explanation: Total: 9 + 7 + 5 + 3 = 24 blocks, shared over 4 towers: 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Tower A gives away 3 blocks and tower B gives away 1: 4 blocks move. Towers C and D receive them (1 and 3).

items.text: The mean mass of 5 parcels is 6 kg.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The 5 parcels weigh {b} kg in all.

parts.label: b
parts.text: 3 of them weigh 4 kg, 9 kg and 7 kg. The other 2 weigh {b} kg together.

items.explanation: Total mass = mean × how many = 6 × 5 = 30 kg. The 3 known parcels weigh 4 + 9 + 7 = 20 kg, so the other 2 weigh 30 − 20 = 10 kg together.

items.text: 4 test scores have a mean of 82. Three of the scores are 78, 90 and 85.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The 4th score is {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A 5th score of {b} keeps the mean at 82.

items.explanation: Total of 4 scores = 4 × 82 = 328. The known scores add to 78 + 90 + 85 = 253. The 4th score is 328 − 253 = 75. A 5th score equal to the mean, 82, keeps the mean at 82.

items.text: The mean of 10, 12 and 14 is 12. Predict, then find what happens when the list changes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Add the value 12. The mean   {circ:goes up|stays the same|goes down}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Add the value 20. The new mean is {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Take away the value 14. The new mean is {b}.

items.explanation: (a) A new value equal to the mean does not change it: the mean stays at 12. (b) 10 + 12 + 14 + 20 = 56, and 56 ÷ 4 = 14. (c) 10 + 12 = 22, and 22 ÷ 2 = 11.

items.text: The median is the middle value when the values are in order. The mode is the value that appears most often.

parts.label: a
parts.text: For 12, 7, 9, 7, 5 the median is {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The mode is {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The mean is {b}.

parts.label: d
parts.text: For 2, 8, 4, 6 the median is {b}.

items.explanation: 5, 7, 7, 9, 12: median 7, mode 7, mean 40 ÷ 5 = 8. 2, 4, 6, 8: the middle two are 4 and 6, so the median is 5.

items.text: A cafe has 7 staff. Their pay in dollars a month is 1500, 1600, 1600, 1700, 1800, 1900 and 9500.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The mean pay is {b} dollars.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The median pay is {b} dollars.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which describes what most staff earn better?   {circ:mean|median}

items.explanation: Total 19600, and 19600 ÷ 7 = 2800. In order the middle (4th) value is 1700. The owner's 9500 pulls the mean up, so the median is more typical.

items.text: The mean mass of 5 children is 40 kg. A 6th child of mass 52 kg joins them.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The 5 children weigh {b} kg in all.

parts.label: b
parts.text: With the 6th child the total is {b} kg.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The new mean is {b} kg.

items.explanation: Total of 5 children = 5 × 40 = 200 kg. With the 6th child: 200 + 52 = 252 kg. New mean = 252 ÷ 6 = 42 kg.

items.text: The bar chart shows the number of stickers 6 pupils have.

parts.label: a
parts.text: They have {b} stickers in all.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The mean is {b} stickers.

parts.label: c
parts.text: {b} pupils have more than the mean.

items.explanation: Total: 14 + 9 + 17 + 12 + 8 + 12 = 72. Mean = 72 ÷ 6 = 12. Above 12: 14 and 17 is 2 pupils. (Two pupils have exactly 12.)

items.text: The list scores holds 7, 9, 3 and 5. A loop adds up the items and the program says the mean.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After the loop, total is {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The program says {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: If the last line says total ÷ 3, it says {b}.

prog: change total by (item i of scores)

items.explanation: i goes 1, 2, 3, 4 and the loop adds 7, 9, 3 and 5: total 24. The last line says 24 ÷ 4 = 6. If it divided by 3 it would say 24 ÷ 3 = 8.

items.text: The mean of 4, 8 and 12 is 8. Change every number in the list in the same way.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Add 5 to every number. The new mean is {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Double every number. The new mean is {b}.

items.explanation: Add 5 to each: 9, 13, 17. 39 ÷ 3 = 13, which is the old mean + 5. Double each: 8, 16, 24. 48 ÷ 3 = 16, which is the old mean × 2.

items.text: Five whole numbers have a mean of 7 and a median of 6. Their only mode is 4, and the largest number is 13.
items.hint: The 2 smallest are 4 and 4. Use the total for the other.
items.explanation: The total is 5 × 7 = 35. The middle number is 6, and the mode 4 is also the smallest, so the first two are 4 and 4: 4, 4, 6, ?, 13. The 4th is 35 − 27 = 8.

items.text: A class has 12 girls and 18 boys. The girls have a mean mass of 40 kg. The boys have a mean mass of 45 kg.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The girls weigh {b} kg in all.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The boys weigh {b} kg in all.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The mean mass of all 30 is {b} kg.

parts.label: d
parts.text: It is more than 42.5 because there are more   {circ:girls|boys}

items.hint: Find each group total first. Then find the total for all 30.
items.explanation: Girls: 12 × 40 = 480 kg. Boys: 18 × 45 = 810 kg. All 30: 480 + 810 = 1290 kg. 1290 ÷ 30 = 43. The mean of the whole class is 43 kg, not 42.5, because there are more boys.

items.text: The mean of 3 numbers is 6.4. Two of them are 5.5 and 7.2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The 3 numbers add up to {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The third number is {b}.

items.hint: Total = mean × how many. Then take away what you know.
items.explanation: The total is 3 × 6.4 = 19.2. The known numbers add to 5.5 + 7.2 = 12.7. The third number is 19.2 − 12.7 = 6.5.

items.text:
Beyond Level 6: Pairing up.
The numbers 7, 12, 17, 22, ..., 102 go up by 5 each time. There are 20 of them.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The 1st and the last add up to {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The 20 numbers make {b} such pairs.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The mean of the 20 numbers is {b}.

items.hint: Pair the 1st with the last, the 2nd with the 2nd last.
items.explanation: The 1st and last add to 7 + 102 = 109. So do the 2nd and the 2nd last (12 + 97). 20 numbers make 10 pairs of 109, so the total is 1090. The mean is 1090 ÷ 20 = 54.5, which is halfway between 7 and 102.

items.text: The list marks holds 4, 8, 6, 10 and 7. This program adds up the items and says the mean.

parts.label: a
parts.text: It says {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: With repeat 4 and ÷ 5 it says {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: With 13 added to the list it says {b}.

prog: change total by (item i of marks)

items.hint: Add up the items the loop reaches. Then divide.
items.explanation: Total 4 + 8 + 6 + 10 + 7 = 35 and 35 ÷ 5 = 7. With repeat 4 the total is only 28 and 28 ÷ 5 = 5.6. With 13 added the total is 48 and 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

items.text:
Beyond Level 6: A frequency table.
In 10 matches a team scored goals as shown.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The team scored {b} goals in all.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The mean number of goals is {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The median number of goals is {b}.

items.hint: 2 matches with 0 goals, 4 with 1 goal: count goals for each column.
items.explanation: Total goals: 0 × 2 + 1 × 4 + 2 × 3 + 3 × 1 = 13. Mean = 13 ÷ 10 = 1.3. In order, the 5th and 6th of the 10 values are both 1, so the median is 1.

items.text: The mean of 6, 10, 2 and 14 is {b}.
For 4, 9, 4, 6, 11 the median is {b} and the mode is {b}.
items.explanation: In order: 4, 4, 6, 9, 11. The middle value is 6, and 4 appears most often.

items.text: 5 numbers have a mean of 6. Four of them are 3, 7, 4 and 9. The fifth is {b}.
The mean of 4 tests is 70. A 5th test score is 80. The new mean is {b}.
items.explanation: The 4 tests total 4 × 70 = 280. With the 5th: 280 + 80 = 360, and 360 ÷ 5 = 72.
